# Lab 20.1: Monitoring Page

## What We Are Going to Do
Read BigQuery's resource utilisation charts for slots, job concurrency, bytes processed and errors, and reproduce one chart with SQL.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Create some load to look at.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --nouse_cache \
    'SELECT company, AVG(fare) FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips` WHERE trip_miles &gt; 5 GROUP BY company' &gt; /dev/null &amp;
done
wait</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[Console] Open Monitoring.** **Administration → Monitoring**. Set the time range to **Last 1 hour** and location **US**.

3. **[Console] Read each chart.**
   - **Slot usage**: slots used over time, split by job type
   - **Job concurrency**: running and queued jobs
   - **Bytes processed** and **bytes billed**
   - **Job errors**: failed jobs by error reason

   Hover over the spike from step 1.

4. **[SQL] Rebuild the slot chart with SQL.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(period_start, MINUTE) AS minute,
  SUM(period_slot_ms) / 1000 / 60 AS avg_slots
FROM `region-us`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_TIMELINE_BY_PROJECT
WHERE job_creation_time &gt; TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 HOUR)
GROUP BY minute
ORDER BY minute;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Open the result's **Chart** tab to draw it.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Slot chart | Spike from 5 parallel queries |
| Concurrency | Running vs pending jobs |
| Errors | Failures grouped by reason |
| SQL | JOBS_TIMELINE gives the same data |
